valuation_philosophy.model_type: Blended AFFO(Distributable Profit)-capitalization / NTA-based cost-of-equity model (REIT), NOT a WACC-based owner-FCF DCF
valuation_philosophy.rationale: Investore is an externally managed, levered NZX large-format-retail REIT (43 properties, ~$1.1bn portfolio, ~40% LVR). Reported NPAT swings on unrealised investment-property fair-value revaluations (FY2021 +$161.3m within a $250.0m profit, FY2023 -$150.2m loss, FY2024 -$67.1m loss) and is not a cash-flow proxy; statutory EPS and P/E are noise and are explicitly excluded as valuation drivers. The company's own disclosed Distributable Profit After Tax (DPAT) -- profit before tax adjusted for non-recurring/non-cash fair-value items, less current tax -- is the owner-earnings base. Crucially, DPAT is measured AFTER interest expense (i.e. it is an equity-level, post-leverage cash flow), so it is capitalized/discounted at the REIT's COST OF EQUITY, never at a blended WACC, and net debt is NEVER subtracted a second time from the resulting value -- doing so would double-count leverage already embedded in DPAT. The reported 'FreeCashFlow' CSV column (OCF less capex) is not used as the valuation base: for a REIT, 'capex' in the cash-flow statement is mostly discretionary property acquisition/development (an investing decision, portfolio recycling), not maintenance capex, and using it would understate distributable capacity by treating growth investment as a cost of running the existing portfolio. EBITDA is undefined for a fair-value-accounted property vehicle (no clean D&A/EBIT split under IAS 40) and is skipped rather than manufactured. Stock-based compensation is verified NIL -- Investore is externally managed by Stride Investment Management Limited (SIML) with no employees of its own, so the standard SBC dilution adjustment is a genuine no-op here (stated explicitly rather than silently skipped). Because per-share Distributable Profit has been essentially FLAT (~8.1-8.4cps) since FY2021, and near-term FY2027 pressure exists from two 2027 bond maturities (IPL020, IPL030) refinancing off low legacy coupons plus hedge roll-off on the 4.2% weighted average cost of debt, the base case models a near-term dip before modest reversion-driven per-share growth resumes -- not smooth compounding. The final valuation blends two independently built estimates 50/50: (1) capitalized Distributable Profit at cost of equity with a P/DP-multiple-based terminal value, and (2) projected book NTA per share at a justified exit P/NTA (reflecting the REIT's persistent trading discount to book through this rate cycle) plus the present value of interim cash dividends. The blended base-case value of ~$1.03 sits just below the current $1.05 price -- a legitimate 'roughly fairly valued, buy for yield' conclusion for a mature, low-growth income REIT trading at a large discount to its own $1.62 NTA, not a manufactured multi-bagger.

warnings: This is a REIT AFFO(Distributable Profit)-capitalization + NTA-based model, not a standard owner-FCF/WACC DCF. Reported NetIncome and statutory EPS are unsuitable growth drivers (fair-value revaluation noise: FY2021 +$161.3m gain-driven profit, FY2023 -$150.2m loss, FY2024 -$67.1m loss).

Distributable Profit is already post-interest (an equity-level cash flow). Net debt is NEVER subtracted from the DCF/entry-price equity value -- doing so would double-count leverage baked into the earnings base.
SBC is verified NIL (external management, no employees) -- the standard owner-FCF SBC deduction is a genuine no-op for this ticker, not an omission.

Per-share Distributable Profit has been essentially flat (8.1-8.4cps) since FY2021 -- this is an income/yield stock, not a compounder. Two bond maturities in FY2027 (IPL020 Aug-2027 2.40% coupon, IPL030 Feb-2027 4.00% coupon) refinancing at materially higher rates, plus roll-off of the 80%-hedged 4.2% weighted average cost of debt, create near-term (FY2027) pressure on distributable profit per share that the base case reflects as a dip, not a straight-line up.
Woolworths NZ concentration (53% of Contract Rental, down from 62%) remains a dominant single-counterparty risk and is priced into the cost-of-equity build via an explicit premium.

External management by SIML/Stride Property Group is a recurring governance cost and conflict (FY26 fees $8.0m = ~26% of distributable profit; FY26 Silverdale Centre acquired directly from cornerstone shareholder/parent Stride Property Limited via related-party vote) -- reflected as a discrete cost-of-equity premium.

Terminal value is 66-74% of equity value across scenarios (AFFO-cap leg), typical for a REIT capitalization model but meaning the valuation is sensitive to the exit-yield/cost-of-equity assumptions (see sensitivity matrix).

Current price is at the BOTTOM of the trailing 10-year FY-end price range ($1.00-$2.26), so the standard '>100% upside while price sits in the upper half of its range' sanity trip does not apply here and was not triggered.

inputs.net_debt_note: Total Debt 511.253m less Cash 4.720m (FY2026). NOT subtracted anywhere in this valuation -- Distributable Profit is already post-interest, so net debt is embedded in the earnings base, not deducted separately.
inputs.sbc_source: Externally managed by Stride Investment Management Limited (SIML) -- Investore has no employees of its own, so stock-based compensation is verified NIL (confirmed by StockBasedComp=0.0 across all history in the Metrics CSV). The owner-FCF SBC adjustment from the skill methodology is therefore a genuine no-op for this ticker.
inputs.last_fcf_note: No owner-FCF figure is used in this model -- Distributable Profit After Tax is the valuation base, capitalized at cost of equity. See valuation_philosophy.
inputs.dilution_source: No formal DRP disclosed as active; modest 0.5%/yr assumed for incidental equity issuance funding acquisitions/recycling (conservative -- FY26 diluted EPS 7.99c vs basic 8.40c already reflects the $62.5m convertible notes' potential dilution, modelled separately as a financing decision, not organic share growth)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: per-share Distributable Profit 5yr CAGR (FY21-26), essentially flat
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Total Distributable Profit grew at a much faster 5yr CAGR (1.08%) and 10yr CAGR (6.38%) than per-share Distributable Profit (0.2%/-1.54%) -- the gap is share-count growth from equity issuance funding acquisitions, not organic per-property earnings growth. Per the skill's per-share discipline, per-share DPS growth (not total DP growth, and not NTA CAGR, which is dominated by cap-rate revaluation swings unrelated to operating performance) is used as the primary driver.
historical_growth.notes: Standard revenue/EPS/equity CAGR selection logic does not apply to this REIT. NetIncome and book equity are dominated by unrealised cap-rate-driven fair-value swings (NTA/share fell from $2.32 FY2022 to $1.57 FY2024 on ~130bp of cap-rate expansion, then recovered to $1.62 FY2026) and are excluded as growth drivers. Per-share Distributable Profit has been range-bound 7.6-8.4 cents for six years (FY2021-FY2026) with essentially zero underlying compounding -- this is the central fact the base case is built around: growth comes from rent-review reversion (4.7% like-for-like FY26) and portfolio recycling, largely offset over the projection horizon by higher-for-longer refinancing costs on two FY2027 bond maturities and hedge roll-off.

cost_of_equity_build.risk_free_rate_note: NZ 10-year government bond, midpoint of 4.2-4.5% range
cost_of_equity_build.beta_note: REIT beta typically below 1.0 given defensive, largely non-discretionary rental income (Woolworths/Bunnings anchors, long WALT), but elevated by ~40% LVR gearing versus an unlevered property beta
cost_of_equity_build.tenant_concentration_premium_note: Woolworths NZ = 53% of Contract Rental (down from 62%, still extreme single-counterparty exposure)
cost_of_equity_build.illiquidity_premium_note: Small-cap NZX listing, market cap ~NZ$396m (377.623m shares x $1.05)
cost_of_equity_build.governance_premium_note: External management by SIML/Stride Property Group: FY26 fees $8.0m (~26% of distributable profit), up from $7.0m FY25; FY26 Silverdale Centre acquired directly from cornerstone shareholder/parent Stride Property Limited (18.8% holder) via related-party shareholder vote -- a structural conflict-of-interest cost not borne by internally managed peers

base.dps_growth_rationale: FY2027 dip reflects IPL020 (Feb/Aug-2027 maturities: IPL030 4.00% coupon Feb-2027, IPL020 2.40% coupon Aug-2027) refinancing at materially higher rates than their legacy coupons plus continued hedge roll-off against the 4.2% weighted average cost of debt (currently 80% hedged, weighted average fixed-rate maturity only ~1.9-2.4yrs); thereafter modest recovery as rent reviews (4.7% like-for-like FY26) and the reduced Woolworths concentration (post-Silverdale/Bunnings New Lynn recycling) support gradual reversion-driven per-share growth, capped below the pre-2022 trend given the mature, largely-full portfolio
base.nta_growth_rationale: Modest capital growth from rent-review-driven property income growth and broadly stable cap rates (WACR held at 6.3% FY25 and FY26); no material further cap-rate compression assumed
base.exit_p_nta_rationale: Historical average P/NTA over FY2017-2026 was 0.815x (max 0.99x, pre-2022 rate-tightening era); 0.75x reflects partial but not full closure of the current 0.645x discount, consistent with REITs trading at persistent discounts through this rate cycle rather than a full re-rating to par

bull.dps_growth_rationale: FY2027 bond refinancing absorbed with minimal drag (OCR cutting cycle continues, lender competition keeps refi spreads tight); fuller rent-review reversion capture, accretive portfolio recycling continues (Silverdale/Bunnings New Lynn-style acquisitions at 6.1-6.8% yields), expanded convenience-retail mandate widens the accretive acquisition pipeline
bull.exit_p_nta_rationale: Discount narrows further toward the FY2019-21 range (0.85-0.99x) as rate-cutting cycle supports cap-rate compression and improved investor depth/liquidity for commercial property (per Chair's May-2026 commentary)

bear.dps_growth_rationale: Renewed inflation/geopolitical shock (flagged live by management in the FY26 Chair's letter) stalls the rate-cutting cycle or reverses it; FY2027 bond refinancing materially more expensive than modelled in base; Woolworths NZ store-network rationalisation or credit-quality deterioration pressures the largest single income line; LVR (already at the top of the 30-40% target band, covenant loosened to 60%) constrains further accretive acquisitions
bear.exit_p_nta_rationale: A repeat, smaller-scale version of the FY23-24 cap-rate expansion dynamic (NTA fell $2.32 to $1.57 over two years) as rates stay higher for longer; discount to NTA persists near current levels or widens modestly

base.note: No net-debt deduction: Distributable Profit is already an equity-level, post-interest cash flow, so subtracting net debt again would double-count leverage

nta_based_leg.methodology: PV of interim cash dividends (discounted at cost of equity) + PV of exit value (projected year-5 NTA per share x justified exit P/NTA x year-5 share count). No net-debt deduction -- NTA per share is already an equity (post-debt) book value.

cross_checks.distributable_profit_capitalization_floo: Current DPS/share (8.13 cps) capitalized in perpetuity at base-case cost of equity (10.5%), zero growth -- represents a floor value assuming no reversion capture, no recycling upside, and no bond-refinancing headwind whatsoever
cross_checks.nta_ceiling_basis: FY2026 book NTA/share -- proxy for replacement/liquidation value; IPL has traded at a persistent, and currently widening, discount to NTA (0.645x FY2026 vs 0.86-0.99x FY2017-21)

entry_price.basis: AFFO-capitalization leg only (base case), consistent with the skill formula. No net-debt adjustment -- Distributable Profit is already post-interest.

base.note: TV_5 is computed using the base-case exit yield (7.5%, i.e. the fair-value assumption a buyer pays at exit) but discounted back to today at the 15% hurdle rate, not the cost of equity. No net-debt deduction, for the same reason as the intrinsic value calc.

sensitivity.matrix_note: AFFO-capitalization leg only. Rows = cost of equity (8.5%-12.5%), Columns = exit Distributable Profit yield (5.5%-9.5%); base-case DPS growth path held constant

sanity_check.note: REIT model: earnings multiples use company-disclosed Distributable Profit per share, not GAAP EPS, because reported NetIncome swings on unrealised fair-value revaluations (FY2021 +$161.3m gain-driven profit of $250.0m total, FY2023 -$150.2m loss, FY2024 -$67.1m loss). P/E and EV/EBITDA are skipped entirely: statutory EPS is not a valuation-relevant multiple for this business, and EBITDA is structurally undefined under IAS 40 fair-value accounting (no clean D&A/EBIT split, confirmed NULL in the Metrics CSV by design). P/NTA uses reported NTA per share (company-disclosed, excludes non-property-related intangibles).

implied_multiples_at_current_price.p_e_note: Skipped: statutory EPS is fair-value-distorted and not a meaningful multiple for this REIT
implied_multiples_at_current_price.ev_ebitda_note: Skipped: no clean EBITDA under IAS 40 fair-value accounting; EBITDA is deliberately NULL in the Metrics CSV

historical_averages_10yr.p_dp_note: P/DP averages inflated by the FY2019-2022 ultra-low-rate era (20-25x); the trip threshold below uses the full 10yr average as the conservative (higher) bar

trip_thresholds.upside_trip: upside >100% while price sits in upper half of 10yr range -- N/A here, current price ($1.05) is at the bottom of the range ($1.00-$2.26)

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Implied P/NTA at the base blended IV (0.634x) is BELOW both the current price's own implied P/NTA (0.648x) and the 10yr historical average (0.815x), and far below the 1.5x-max trip threshold (1.486x). Implied P/DP (12.64x) is below the current price's own implied P/DP (12.92x) and well below the 10yr average (17.77x) and the 2x-average trip threshold (35.5x). Current price sits at the bottom of its 10yr range, so the peak-extrapolation/upside trip does not apply, and in any case base-case upside is negative (-2.14%). The model is conservative relative to history by construction: DPS growth path dips before recovering (vs a flat extrapolation), exit P/NTA (0.75x base) is below the 10yr average (0.815x), and exit P/DP (13.33x) sits in the bottom third of the historical 12.9-25.6x range.
